seats: a secular academic scholar of the Bible

fixes.row: The cup: "This is My blood", "drink My blood", "a participation in the blood of Christ"
fixes.why: John 6:53-56 never mentions a cup or the Supper (the note itself says readers part on whether it does). Filing them under 'The cup' reads the Supper into the Capernaum saying by row structure, which the note then disclaims.
fixes.fix: Relabel to 'The cup and the drinking of blood: "This is My blood", "drink My blood"' and add to the note that John 6 has no cup and no Supper in its verses and sits here for the words 'drink the blood'; or give John 6:53-56 a short row of its own.

fixes.why: John 1:13 reads 'children born not of blood' (plural αἱμάτων, descent), with no 'flesh and blood' phrase; the note lists it as an instance of 'the phrase for a human being', which it is not. Gal 1:16 'did not consult flesh and blood' is fine but is not quoted.
fixes.fix: Move John 1:13 out into its own short note line ('and "not of blood", of descent, John 1:13') or relabel the row 'Flesh and blood: a human being; "not of blood"'. Reword the note so John 1:13 is not called the phrase.

fixes.row: Blood in the worship of other gods: "libations of blood", sons and daughters, the prophets of Baal, pig's blood
fixes.why: Isa 66:3 is a series of similes ('whoever presents a grain offering is like one who offers pig's blood'), about offerings made by those who chose their own ways; the only idol in it is 'blesses an idol'. It is not blood given to other gods, so the label says more than the verse.
fixes.fix: Move Isa 66:3 to 'Blood in the rites of sacrifice' with a note line, or keep it here but add to the note that the verse is a comparison and does not name another god's altar.

fixes.row: Atonement and forgiveness beside blood: "it is the blood that makes atonement", "without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness"
fixes.why: Heb 10:4 says it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins. Filed under a label of what the blood does, with no sign that it denies this, it reads as a witness for the label. Hebrews' argument (the old blood cannot, the better blood does) is the arc the teacher would want to see.
fixes.fix: Keep the verse but quote it in the note ('Heb 10:4: "impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins"') so the row shows the verse says the opposite of the label for the old rites, and the page takes no side on what that implies.

fixes.row: Redeemed, purchased, released: "by Your blood You purchased for God"
fixes.why: Ps 72:14 is a king who redeems (גאל) the poor from oppression, 'for their blood is precious in his sight'; it is not blood as the price. Under a heading of 'by Your blood You purchased' it is heard through the New Testament. It is already in the avenged row where it fits.
fixes.fix: Remove Ps 72:14 from this row (leave it in the avenged row) or, if kept, reword the note to say the blood there is the poor's life, precious to the king, not the price paid.

fixes.row: Blood in war and in the LORD's judgment: the slain, arrows drunk with blood, blood as high as the bridles
fixes.why: 2 Sam 20:12 is Amasa lying in his blood on the road after Joab killed him: a killing by a man, not war or the LORD's judgment, and the note presents it as one of the places 'where kings and the wicked fell'.
fixes.fix: Move 2 Sam 20:12 to 'Shedding blood' and drop it from the war note.

fixes.row: 'His blood', 'His own blood', 'Your blood': the verse names no one
fixes.why: All seven verses already sit in rows 17 and 18 (and Rom 3:25 in 15). The row divides by grammar (a pronoun or a name) rather than by what the text says, so it cuts the same verses apart a third time and makes the Christ row look like the 'named' set against an 'unnamed' set. Its note also supplies the names from nearby verses, which is an inference the page otherwise avoids.
fixes.fix: Merge into 'The blood of Christ, of Jesus, of the Son, of the Lamb' (row 21), keeping the Acts 20:28 note, and say in the note that some verses carry the pronoun only. This also brings the hub to 23 rows.

fixes.row: "The life is in the blood": not to be eaten or drunk; Shedding blood; Blood avenged and required
fixes.why: Gen 9:4-6 is one speech (the life is in the blood, the LORD requires it, 'by man his blood will be shed') and the rows cut it into three. The story's own arc, from Noah's blood commandment through Abel and Sinai to the rest, is the hub's strongest thread, and nothing points the reader from one cut to the next.
fixes.fix: Add a closing sentence to each of the three notes: 'Gen 9:4-6 is one speech; see also the rows ...' naming the other two rows. No verse moves.

fixes.row: "The life is in the blood": not to be eaten or drunk
fixes.why: The label 'not to be eaten or drunk' assumes Acts 15's 'and from blood' is eaten blood, which the note says readers dispute; and David's water 'the blood of the men' is not about eating blood at all. A label should say only what the verses say.
fixes.fix: Relabel to '"The life is in the blood": eating and drinking blood' (neutral), keep the note's disclaimer.

fixes.row: Blood as a sign: water to blood, the moon to blood, water that looked like blood, blood in the visions
fixes.why: Of these, 2 Kgs 3:22 is a trick of the light on water, not a sign, and the Nile verses are the plague. 'Sign' is true of Exod 4:9 and Joel, not of every verse; 'blood in the visions' is vague.
fixes.fix: Relabel to 'Water turned to blood, the moon turned to blood: in the plagues, in the prophets, in Revelation' and keep 2 Kgs 3:22 with a note line that it is an appearance.

worker_points.point: 1. What the blood does (rows 15-18, alphabetical, no ranking)
worker_points.why: Alphabetical order is fine and the notes say so, but Heb 10:4 (see fixes) and Ps 72:14 (OT heard through the NT heading) need the changes noted. The ἱλαστήριον gloss list is fair.
The note states both readings of 'His own blood' and does not choose. Merging row 22 into 21 keeps this note.

worker_points.point: 3. The cup and the covenant (rows 19 and 20)
worker_points.why: The covenant row is fine. The cup row's label carries John 6 into the Supper (see fixes); the Luke 22:20 manuscript note is correct.

worker_points.point: 4. The life is in the blood / eating of blood (row 2)
worker_points.why: The note is balanced; the label presumes the eaten-blood reading for Acts 15 (see fixes).

From a text-and-history seat the wording is enough: it places Pilate's verse beside it, says what the verse says of those who spoke it, and no more. The cross-reference from the blood-guilt row is good. The rabbi and the African American believer seats should confirm.
Row 21's rule (the verse names Christ, Jesus, the Son or the Lamb) is clean. Row 22 duplicates content and borrows names from neighbouring verses; merge it into 21.
The three readings of whose blood are stated, and the hub takes no side.
Quoted whole in the Abel row and listed again in the Christ row; no side taken on the 'better word'.
Num 35, Ps 9:12, Rev 6:10 and 19:2 are set side by side; 2 Sam 3:27 and 1 Chr 22:8 are kept. The goel not being equated with the redeemer is rightly noted.
Old Testament verses lead each row and the Hebrews verses follow; the notes say the relation is read differently and take no side.
Isa 66:3 is a simile about offerings and does not name another god's altar (see fixes).

missing.what: Exod 4:24-26 'bridegroom of blood' sits in 'Every other use', but it comes in the same chapter as the sign of water to blood (4:9) and just before the Passover blood; a literary reader would want a pointer from the sign or Passover row.
Gen 37:31 (Joseph's robe dipped in blood) is the deceit that begins the exile story and echoes the shed-blood row (Gen 37:22, 26 are already there); it sits only in 'Every other use'.

Isa 63:3 (the winepress, 'their blood spattered my garments') is a different Hebrew word but is the Old Testament source image for Rev 14:20 and 19:13; the hub could name it under Other words so the reader sees the link without it being called the same word.

examples_checked: 21 of 24 rows' examples show their label; the three that do not fit exactly: the cup row (John 6 has no cup), the other-gods row (Isa 66:3 is a simile), and the flesh-and-blood row (John 1:13 is 'not of blood', not the phrase). Read in the Berean: 2 Sam 20:12, Heb 10:4, Ps 72:14, John 1:13, Isa 66:3, Ezek 35:6, plus the notes' quotations in the built file.
summary: A careful hub whose notes keep the traditions' disputes out of the verses and whose order lets the story run from Abel through the rites to Hebrews. It ships after fixes: a handful of labels say more than their verses (the cup and John 6, Acts 15, John 1:13, Isa 66:3), two verses sit under headings that hear the Old Testament through the New (Ps 72:14, Heb 10:4 without its negation), and row 22 should merge into row 21.
